cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, starts building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. The spot is Mount Moriah. And friend, this isn't some random lot he found scrolling his phone at midnight.

cards.question: Solomon builds the house of the LORD on Mount Moriah. What had happened on that mountain before?

answers.text: The LORD had appeared to David there
David had been anointed king there

cards.question: True or false: Solomon's building spot was the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, and David had already prepared it.

cards.text: Solomon breaks ground on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. The foundation goes down sixty cubits long and twenty wide, by the old standard.

Then the GOLD starts: the inside of the portico, the main room, the beams, the thresholds, the walls, even the DOORS. Friend, the fanciest thing in my old junk drawer was a coupon that expired years ago.

cards.question: With gold on every wall, Solomon adds carvings too. What does he carve on the temple walls?

cards.text: Then comes the Most Holy Place, twenty cubits by twenty, and the inside alone gets six HUNDRED talents of fine gold. In there, Solomon makes two cherubim of sculptured work and overlays them with gold too.

cards.question: Each of the two cherubim in the Most Holy Place stretches out two wings. One wing touches the temple wall, and the other touches the ___ of the other cherub.
True or false: The two cherubim in the Most Holy Place stand facing each other.

cards.text: Then Solomon makes the veil from blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven right into it. Walls, room, now the curtain: this man found his theme and he is NOT letting go.
Out front, he makes two pillars, thirty-five cubits high together, each with a five-cubit capital on top. He puts chainwork on top and fastens a hundred pomegranates into it.

cards.question: Solomon sets up the two pillars in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. Then he does something extra for each pillar. What?

answers.text: He carves a psalm on it
He sets a lamp on it

cards.question: Solomon names the pillar on the south ___ and the pillar on the north ___.

cards.text: Now the furnishings, starting with a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty wide and ten HIGH. Friend, that's not an altar, that's a whole floor plan.
Then he makes the Sea of cast metal: round, ten cubits rim to rim, five high, with two rows of ox figures cast right below the rim. Not the Tub, not the Big Bowl, the SEA.

cards.question: The Sea doesn't sit on the ground. It rests on twelve ___, three facing each direction.

cards.text: The Sea holds three thousand baths. Then Solomon makes ten basins for washing, five on the south side and five on the north, and the parts of the burnt offering get rinsed in them.

cards.question: The ten basins are for rinsing the parts of the burnt offering. So who uses the Sea for washing?
True or false: Solomon makes ten gold lampstands and puts all ten together on the north side of the temple.

cards.text: Then ten tables, placed five and five AGAIN, plus a hundred gold bowls. Then the courtyard of the priests and the large court, with bronze on the doors.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon puts the Sea at the northwest corner.

cards.text: Huram, the craftsman the king of Tyre sent (2 Chronicles 2:13), finishes his work: the pillars, the network, four hundred pomegranates, the stands, the basins, the Sea and its oxen, the pots, shovels and forks, all polished bronze. They're cast in clay molds on the plain of the Jordan.

cards.question: Solomon makes all these bronze articles in great abundance. What's the result?

answers.text: No one could figure out the weight
It used up every mine in Israel

cards.text: Bronze outside, gold inside: Solomon makes the golden altar and the tables for the house of God. Friend, the only gold I own is the base I'm standing on, and I am NOT stepping off it.

cards.question: What gets placed on the tables Solomon makes for the house of God?
The lampstands of pure gold and their lamps burn in front of the inner ___.

cards.text: Last comes the rest in purest gold: flowers, lamps, tongs, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, censers, and the gold doors to the Most Holy Place and the main hall. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't done.

findings.problem: Almost the whole passage is the temple's building plans and furnishings list. prep-walkthrough.md lists 'building plans, like the tabernacle or the temple' as a long stretch that gets one summary story card and no choice cards, and says 'A stretch never gets a stop of its own.' The walkthrough instead spreads 3:3-4:22 over two stops and asks many detail questions: the carved cherubim, the wings, which way the cherubim face, what the Sea rests on, where the lampstands go, the Sea's corner, the Bread of the Presence and the inner sanctuary. Only a few moments clearly move the passage forward: the site and its history (3:1), the start date (3:2), the pillar names (3:17), Huram finishing his work (4:11-16) and the bronze too heavy to weigh (4:18). The docs don't say what to do when the long stretch is most of the passage.
findings.question: When a passage is almost entirely a long stretch, like the temple's building plans, should Prep still ask choice cards about the details? Or should it sum up the building in a card or two and ask only about the few moving moments, even if that makes the passage too short to fill a stop?

findings.problem: Most of stop 1's choice cards can only be answered by luck. Card 3 (the threshing floor of Ornan, a true or false with no setup), card 6 (what is carved on the walls), card 12 (that each pillar gets a name) and card 13 (Jachin and Boaz) have no story card giving context to reason from. On card 9, the setup in card 8 (wings touching each other's wings) points the baker toward the wrong answer, 'facing each other.' That leaves card 8, and maybe card 2, as the only informed guesses out of 7.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The true or false about the Sea's corner (northwest) is a coin flip. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason about where the Sea goes. It's also a minor placement detail the baker doesn't need to understand the passage.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The blank in 'in front of the inner ___' tests the exact BSB wording ('inner sanctuary'). The baker hasn't seen that wording. Earlier cards only call the room 'the Most Holy Place,' so the baker can't reason out the blank from its meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke 'that's not an altar, that's a whole floor plan' doesn't click. A floor plan is a drawing, not a size, so the image doesn't match 'this is huge.' It also depends on the baker knowing how big twenty cubits is, which the card never says.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
